verdict_rationale: Each participant restated or acknowledged the other's position and still preferred a different launch approach. A and B both described the remaining difference as how much risk the extra week is worth.

shared_ground.text: Both explicitly stated that they want a safe launch and agreed that they differ on how much risk the week is worth.

evidence.quote: We both want a safe launch, and we disagree about how much risk the week is worth

insights.title: Full rollout versus a 10% start
insights.observation: A proposed a full rollout on Monday and B proposed starting with 10%. Each acknowledged the other's argument (T05, T06, T08) and kept their own preference.
insights.hypothesis: One possible reading is that A and B weigh the cost of a one-week delay and the risk of untested load behaviour differently, with the pilot evidence read differently.

evidence.quote: the pilot had 5,000 users and no retry failures
I just don’t think 5,000 users is representative of Monday morning traffic
I’d rather take the risk than lose the week

insights.why_it_matters: The launch plan cannot proceed until the difference in acceptable risk is decided by someone.
unknowns: What retry or load data exists beyond the pilot.
How large the cost of the extra week is in practice.
alternative_explanations: The disagreement may be settled by additional load-test data rather than by weighing preferences.
insights.clarification_question: What evidence about load behaviour would each of you need to see to be comfortable with a given rollout size?

A.text: A proposes rolling out to all users on Monday, citing the pilot numbers and the cost of waiting.

evidence.quote: roll the new checkout out to all users on Monday

evidence.quote: I think that’s enough evidence to go

A.text: A prefers accepting the risk over losing a week to a phased rollout.

evidence.quote: I’d rather take the risk than lose the week

B.text: B is concerned that payment retries at full volume could prevent a clean rollback.

differ: Whether the pilot evidence is sufficient for a full rollout.
Whether the one-week cost of a phased rollout is worth the reduced risk.
overlap: Both say the checkout design itself is not the issue (B in T04; A's question in T03 was confirmed by B).

power.title: Who makes the final call
power.observation: B asked who breaks the tie and A answered 'Probably Rina' and said they would set up a call. Neither participant stated that they hold the decision themselves.
power.hypothesis: One possible reading is that the decision sits with a third person, tentatively named.

evidence.quote: Probably Rina, since it touches both our areas

unknowns: Whether Rina has agreed to decide.
Whether B accepts Rina as the decision owner.

power.title: Positions and objections raised by both
power.observation: Both participants stated positions and objections. A asked B to confirm the concern and B restated their preference after A's counter-argument.
power.hypothesis: One possible reading is that both had room to state their views in this conversation; one conversation cannot establish a pattern.

evidence.quote: worried about retries under load, not about the checkout design itself

unknowns: Whether this reflects how they usually interact.

open_questions.question: Who will decide the launch approach, and has that person agreed to?

next_steps.text: Hold the short call with the named decision-maker and bring each side's evidence on load behaviour and the cost of the extra week.

rejected_candidates.title: Undefined meaning of 'enough evidence'
rejected_candidates.reason: B directly addressed it in T06 (representativeness of the pilot), so the difference is a stated disagreement rather than an undefined term.
